ONDCP TEAMS WITH LYCOS TO PROMOTE DRUG PREVENTION MESSAGES TO KIDS, PARENTS, AND TEACHERS

Leading Internet Network Joins Pioneering Online Drug Education Effort

(Washington, D.C.) The White House Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP) today announced an alliance with Lycos, Inc. (www.lycos.com), a leading Internet network. The partnership, a component of ONDCP's National Youth Anti-Drug Media Campaign, will maximize the reach and visibility of the Media Campaign's interactive drug education resources, including the youth-oriented www.freevibe.com and the family-focused www.theantidrug.com.
See
The Village Voice Pans Freevibe Prohibitionist Propaganda Site,
But Doesn’t Understand Its Role In Maintaining Marijuana Prohibition
and
Disney Sponsored Prohibitionist Propaganda Site
Tells Kids That Marijuana Causes Heart Problems;
The War On Children Escalates

The announcement coincides with the kick-off of the Media Campaign's " What's Your Anti-Drug? " initiative, a multi-million dollar effort that encourages kids to share their reasons for avoiding drugs (www.whatsyourantidrug.com).
See
Drug Czar Returns To Party Line,
Opposes Including Ads Warning Kids About Alcohol

" Our collaboration with the Lycos Network provides the Media Campaign with a powerful vehicle for informing kids, parents, and teachers about our valuable online drug education resources, " said ONDCP Director Barry McCaffrey. " We need to reach our kids with engaging drug prevention messages where they are spending an increasing amount of their time—online. To accomplish this goal, we must work with leading Internet companies like Lycos to capture the attention of today's tech-savvy audience. "

As part of the Media Campaign efforts, the Lycos Network will use its award-winning children's Web site Lycos Zone (www.lycoszone.com) to promote a number of ONDCP's drug prevention resources to kids, parents, and teachers. Through this unpaid alliance, Lycos Zone will assist the Media Campaign with its goal of generating youth-to-youth dialogue about drug prevention by developing a page dedicated to the recently launched " What's Your Anti-Drug? " initiative. In addition, Lycos will feature ONDCP resources within the Parents Zone and Teacher Zone sections of Lycos Zone.

" We are happy to showcase ONDCP's important drug prevention messages and content, " said Bob Davis, President and CEO of Lycos, Inc. " The Lycos Network is committed to providing children and families with access to quality, expert-approved resources on a variety of topics.

(MarijuanaNews note: In NORML’s weekly press release, Allen St. Pierre, NORML Foundation Executive Director, said " Expert-approved resources? " " Doesn't Lycos mean to say 'government approved resources.'

Marijuana law reform advocates should send Lycos an email and inform them that they are boycotting Lycos and its advertisers as long as they serve as a propaganda arm of the drug czar's office. "

Founded in 1995, Lycos, Inc. is a leading Web media company and owner of the Lycos Network, one of the most visited hubs on the Internet, reaching nearly one out of every two U.S. Web users. The Lycos Network is composed of Lycos.com, Tripod, WhoWhere, Angelfire, MailCity, HotBot, HotWired, Wired News, Webmonkey, Sonique, Quote, Gamesville, Lycos Zone and Matchmaker. Headquartered near Boston in Waltham, Mass., Lycos, Inc. is a global Internet leader with a major presence throughout the U.S., Europe, Asia, Canada and Latin America.

In 1998, with bipartisan support of the Congress and the President, ONDCP created the National Youth Anti-Drug Media Campaign, an effort designed to educate and empower all youth to reject illicit drugs. The Campaign relies on ads developed by the Partnership for a Drug-Free America.

Counting on an unprecedented blend of public and private partnerships, non-profit community service organizations, volunteerism, and youth-to-youth communications, the Campaign is designed to reach Americans of diverse backgrounds wherever they work, learn, live, or play.
